name: LinkedIn Insight Tag (conversion pixel on other sites)
plain: A script and pixel on advertisers' sites that reports visits and actions back to LinkedIn.
meaning: Lets LinkedIn see which pages a person visits across other sites, tie it to their member profile if logged in, and use it for ads, retargeting and measurement.

access.persistence: Cookies bcookie 1 year, bscookie 1 year, lidc 24 hours, li_gc and li_mc 6 months, lms_ads and lms_analytics 30 days
steps: Advertiser installs the tag with a partner ID
Browser sends page URL, referrer, IP, user agent and timestamp to LinkedIn
If a member is logged in, the event can be tied to the member
Identifiers dropped in 7 days, pseudonymous data deleted within 180 days (LinkedIn help)

limits.headline: Can tell LinkedIn when you visit or act on an advertiser's site
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you open a page that has the LinkedIn tag
can: Report each page you view on sites that use the tag
Report actions such as sign ups or purchases
Link the visit to your LinkedIn account when the browser has a LinkedIn cookie
Help the advertiser build ad audiences from visitors
cannot: Run on sites that do not include the tag
See activity in other apps or sites without the tag
Work if the tag or its cookies are blocked
Know who you are if you never use LinkedIn on that browser
limits.reach_label: Pages and actions on tagged sites
limits.differs: Blocking third party cookies in Safari and Firefox limits the link to your account.

story.what_it_is: A script on other companies' sites that tells LinkedIn which pages you visited.

marketing.name: Insight Tag
marketing.pitch: LinkedIn pitches it as a lightweight script that helps marketers measure conversions, retarget visitors and learn about their audience.

story.for_you: You never see it. When you visit a company's site, a small script tells LinkedIn which page you opened. If you are logged in, LinkedIn can link it to your profile, and use it to show you ads.
story.for_makers: Advertisers want proof that spend led to action, and a way to find visitors again. The Insight Tag counts conversions, builds audiences from site visits and shows who the visitors are by job and company. LinkedIn gets a view of work related web habits that few others have.

use_cases.example: You read a cloud software pricing page, close it, and later see that vendor's ad on your LinkedIn feed.
A marketer sees which job titles and companies visit a pricing page, and which campaign brought them.
A sales team spots that three people from the same bank read their security page this week and alerts the rep.
A university sees which ad drove a master's program inquiry, and what job titles the visitors held.
A webinar host counts signups per ad and sends the best performing posts more budget.
Because it runs on many sites, some browsers now treat it as a tracker. Safari beta reportedly limits its data.

risks: Tied to your real profile when logged in

technical_bounds: Safari ITP and Firefox ETP limit third party cookie lifetimes
Consent is required in EU/UK (Designated Countries) per LinkedIn
Does not read the 48 fingerprint features (no evidence found)

linkedin.how: Insight Tag sends URL, referrer, IP, user agent and timestamp; LinkedIn help page a427660 documents it. No evidence found that it sends fingerprint features.
